publication.affiliations: School of Business, International University, VNU-HCM; FPT University, Ho Chi Minh City Campus
publication.abstract: Strategic sourcing has been recognized for its significance in enhancing sourcing performance across industries, including apparel. This study investigates its function within Vietnam's apparel industry and its contribution to global sourcing competitiveness, where outsourcing drives supply chain efficiency. The research measures strategic sourcing and its core components of the relationships of buyer-supplier, supplier evaluation, and sourcing performance from the perspective of multinational apparel buyers. Based on a theory-driven strategic management model integrating resource and relationship-based views, the study identifies and analyzes four key constructs. We conducted interviews and a large-scale survey of Vietnamese apparel firms, yielding 189 valid responses from 245 distributed. The model was tested using Cronbach's alpha, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM). Results affirm that strategic sourcing strengthens supplier evaluation and buyer-supplier relationships, both of which contribute to improved sourcing performance with managerial implications for strategic sourcing practices in Vietnam's apparel industry.
publication.finding: Strategic sourcing strengthens supplier evaluation and buyer-supplier relationships, and both improve sourcing performance.

phd.title: Proposed doctoral research (PhD)
phd.name: The Relationship Between Corporate Social Responsibility and Supplier Selection Decisions in the Global Garment Supply Chain: The Case of Vietnam
phd.summary: Examines how the economic, social, environmental and governance dimensions of CSR/ESG influence international buyers' supplier-selection decisions, integrating a systematic literature review, an empirical investigation of buyer-side sourcing stakeholders and garment manufacturers in Vietnam, and a multi-criteria decision framework.
